text:
Colorado is 9-6-2, which undersells it. The Avalanche have taken 54.69% of the expected goals (the quality of chances for and against), and our numbers have them about a point short of where the play says they should be. A 93% playoff chance and a 104-point projection are the better guide.

The top line is doing exactly what you'd expect. Nathan MacKinnon, Martin Necas and Artturi Lehkonen have outscored teams 18-9 at 5-on-5, and Lehkonen has 11 points in his last 10. Cale Makar and Devon Toews have taken 58% of the expected goals together.

The leak is in goal. Colorado's goalies have allowed 6.7 more goals than the shots deserved, wiping out much of the 9.7-goal edge the shooters have built. The power play is another sore spot: Evan Rawal of the Denver Gazette watched Nashville's create more good looks in a minute than Colorado usually does, though our expected-goals rate for the Avs' power play is respectable.

Rawal also reported Jared Bednar calling Zachary L'Heureux's absence "long-term, for sure," with no timeline. If the goaltending reaches league average, this team pulls away in the Central.
headline: Avalanche win the chances, not yet the table
